how.h: Meridian writes every step before sending it.
how.s1.p: A single “pay” call, whatever PSP sits behind it. Same reference, same result, even if the request is sent twice.
how.s2.p: Each step is recorded in a chained, signed journal before it reaches the PSP, with one idempotency key per step.
how.s3.h: The outcome is guaranteed and provable
how.s3.p: If anything drops, Meridian resumes from the journal and recovers the real outcome. Every payment ends with a verifiable proof.
guar.r1.b: Keeps the payment “in progress”, never “failed”, and queries the PSP
guar.r2.b: Replays with the same idempotency key
guar.r3.b: Another instance resumes from the shared journal
guar.r4.b: Fails over to the backup PSP, only if nothing was sent
guar.r5.b: Returns the real outcome and allows a refund
ind.h: Wherever people pay, with or without a cashier.
ind.1.p: Ordering kiosks and tills, one connection for every franchised brand.
ind.2.p: The merchant keeps their PSP; the vendor keeps the sale.
ind.3.p: Remote terminals, unstable networks: guaranteed recovery makes the difference.
ind.4.p: Pre-authorisation, final amount, proof for every session.
ind.5.p: Several countries, several PSPs, a single integration.
ind.6.p: Small amounts, high volumes, zero double-charge disputes.

neutral.p: A neutral technical layer: no PSP owns it, none is promoted. The merchant keeps the choice.
close.h: Watch Meridian handle an outage live, in 30 seconds.

psp.conf.p: Your module runs the eight failure scenarios against your sandbox: lost response, network drop, crash, late cancellation. The report is the condition for publication.

pb.h: Today, every PSP is an integration project.
pb.1.a: A merchant arrives with their PSP. You haven't integrated it: the sale is lost, or it's a new development and certification project.
pb.1.b: With Meridian, the PSP is in the catalogue. You select it in the console, without a line of code.
pb.2.a: The network drops during authorisation. The till shows “failed”, the customer pays again, and you handle the double-charge dispute.
pb.2.b: Meridian keeps the payment “in progress”, recovers the real outcome from the PSP, and charges only once.
pb.3.a: You expand to Germany or Belgium. New protocols, new local payment methods, a new project.
pb.3.b: ZVT, nexo, girocard, Bancontact, TWINT: already supported, country by country.
code.h: Five calls. The same code for every PSP.
code.p: Pay, check status, cancel, refund, get the receipt. The SDK handles retries, timeouts and lost responses. Switching PSP means changing a setting, not your code.
flow.n4: Backup, only if nothing was sent
flow.cap: A payment never leaves Meridian without being written to the journal. After an outage, recovery starts from the journal, not from a guess.
guar.stat: 0 double charges across 200 random failure sequences, on every release.
faq.1.a: No. Meridian is a technical provider: it holds no funds and signs no contracts with merchants. Payments are executed by the PSP the merchant chose, under its own licence.
faq.2.q: Does card data go through Meridian?
faq.2.a: No. The card is read by the terminal and processed by the PSP. Meridian only receives the result, the brand and the last 4 digits for the receipt.
faq.3.q: What happens if Meridian goes down?
faq.3.a: Several instances share the same journal. If one fails mid-payment, another resumes from the last written step and recovers the real outcome from the PSP. This scenario is tested on every release.
faq.4.q: Do my Concert or ZVT tills need to change?
faq.4.a: No. You point the till at Meridian instead of the terminal; the messages stay the same.
faq.5.a: Stripe Terminal, currently being validated on its sandbox. Each new PSP arrives as a declarative module, published after passing the eight failure scenarios.
faq.6.a: PSPs pay a distribution fee on the volume Meridian brings them, at the same rate for all. A share goes back to the vendor on every payment made by its merchants. The merchant pays nothing extra to Meridian, and Meridian never touches the funds.
x.h1:
The network drops.
The payment goes through.
x.sub: Meridian connects any till to any terminal or PSP: in the cloud, locally, or without touching the till. Every payment goes through, exactly once.
x.wait: Network down. Payment held in progress.
st.1.p: The till calls Meridian. Before writing to the PSP, Meridian records the step in its journal.
st.2.p: An ordinary till shows “failed”. The customer pays again. The double charge is done.
st.3.p: The payment stays “in progress”. When the network returns, Meridian asks the PSP with the same key and recovers the real outcome.
st.4.p: The customer is charged once. The receipt prints, with its signed proof.
s3.p: Five calls. The same code, whatever the merchant's PSP. Switching PSP becomes a setting.
s4.p: Concert in France, ZVT in Germany, nexo everywhere. Point the till at Meridian; nothing else changes.
s5.h: Eight countries. The way they pay.
s5.p: Cards, and the payment methods each country actually uses.
s6.p: The PSP keeps the contract, KYC, funds and its fees. Meridian sees neither the card nor the money: only the result, and its proof.
s7.p: No sign-up. A real payment, a real outage, thirty seconds.

bt.h: Built for POS software vendors. Not for a bank, not for a single PSP.
bt.p: Five commitments that banking platforms, enterprise orchestrators and single-PSP offers do not make.
bt.1.p: Five calls, one SDK: the till connects to a PSP or to the in-store terminal, and your Concert, ZVT or nexo tills work as they are.
bt.2.p: PSPs pay for distribution; you receive a share of every transaction your merchants make.
bt.3.p: Every payment is proven by a signed journal. A double charge caused by Meridian is refunded.
bt.4.p: The same published rate card for every PSP. No PSP and no bank among our shareholders.
bt.5.p: Each PSP publishes its module and its failure-test report. Nothing gets in without passing the 8 scenarios.
bt.6.h: The PSP you choose, till by till
bt.6.p: A primary and a backup PSP per till, with the live status of each connection. Switching PSP takes no development.
nc.h: Meridian carries the instructions. Never the money.
nc.p: The till sends the payment order to Meridian, which passes it to the chosen PSP. Funds go straight from the PSP to the merchant; the contract, KYC and fees stay with the PSP.

faq.7.a: That no payment is charged twice because of Meridian. Every payment is proven by a signed journal; a double charge caused by Meridian is refunded, under the terms of the contract.
faq.8.a: No. Meridian is a connector and a catalogue: the software vendor or the merchant picks each till's PSP from the catalogue and plugs it in, with an optional backup PSP used only if the first cannot be reached. Meridian never picks the PSP on the merchant's behalf.
v10.w3.p: A share of every transaction for the vendor.
md2.p: Installed or online till, in-store terminal or cloud PSP, existing protocol or new integration: the same five calls, the same signed journal, the same proof.
md2.1.p: The till calls Meridian, which drives the terminal through the PSP's API.
md2.2.p: The installed till talks to the in-store Meridian agent, which drives the terminal over Caisse-AP, ZVT or nexo. Works without internet.
md2.3.h: In-store terminal, from an online till
md2.3.p: The SaaS till calls the Meridian API, which relays to the in-store agent over an outbound connection: no port to open.
md2.4.p: The till keeps its Concert, ZVT or nexo messages: Meridian presents itself as its terminal.
md2.5.p: Accept without a terminal using the PSP's Tap to Pay; Meridian tracks and proves every payment.
nc2.h: What your till no longer has to code.
nc2.p: Driving a terminal takes far more than a payment call. The Meridian agent and API handle it, whatever the protocol or PSP.

v11.pill: Payment connector for tills and kiosks
v11.h1: Connect any payment terminal to your till.
v11.lede: One integration, on the local network or from the cloud. Meridian handles the session, waiting for the result, dropped connections and busy terminals: you code five calls, your merchants keep their PSP.
v11.w1.p: The same code, installed or online till.
v11.w2.p: Even when the terminal's response gets lost.
v11.w3.p: In-store terminals, with no driver to write.
v11.try: Simulation: connect a PSP to a till
v11.proof.p: Meridian keeps the payment in progress and recovers its real outcome: zero double charges across 25 random failure sequences, replayed on every release.
v11.mkt.p: POS and business software vendors serve local commerce across the Nordics, the UK, France, Germany, Austria, Switzerland, Italy and Eastern Europe. Each one has to connect its merchants' terminals and PSPs.
v11.mkt.src: Source: Bain & Company and Nexi, February 2026
v11.uc.p: What software vendors and resellers deal with today, and what changes with Meridian.
v11.uc.1.sit: Its restaurants already have a bank terminal or a PSP's terminal.
v11.uc.1.today: The till lives in the cloud and cannot see the restaurant's terminal: amounts keyed in twice, end-of-day gaps, lost customers.
v11.uc.1.with: The Meridian agent in the restaurant links the terminal to the cloud till over an outbound connection. The amount leaves the till, the outcome comes back.
v11.uc.2.sit: A terminal in every kiosk, retailers with different banks.
v11.uc.2.today: One driver per terminal and protocol, and payments stuck when the internet drops.
v11.uc.2.with: The kiosk talks to the agent locally, which drives the terminal over Caisse-AP, ZVT or nexo, even without internet.
v11.uc.3.sit: Thirty points of sale to equip, with different terminals and PSPs from one customer to the next.
v11.uc.3.today: An integration to redo for every project, or a specialist integrator to pay for every till.
v11.uc.3.with: One installation procedure, one console for every site, the same connection whatever the terminal.
v11.uc.4.sit: A new customer arrives with a PSP the till does not support.
v11.uc.4.today: Turn the customer away, or start an integration that takes weeks.
v11.uc.4.with: The PSP is picked from the catalogue and connected with no development, with an optional backup PSP.
v11.md4.p: The till keeps its Concert, ZVT or nexo messages and talks to Meridian as it would to a terminal; Meridian sends the payment through the chosen PSP.
v11.bt.p: Five commitments you can check from the very first payment.
v11.bt2.p: Revenue sharing with PSPs is being set with the pilot programme partners: you keep the relationship, Meridian does the connecting.
v11.bt3.p: Every payment is recorded in a signed journal that you can check step by step.
v11.bt4.p: The same terms for every PSP in the catalogue. No PSP and no bank among our shareholders.
v11.md1c: Revenue sharing set with the first partner PSPs
v11.md2a: The same terms for every PSP
v11.calc.h: What your merchants' payments could earn you.
v11.calc.n: An order of magnitude, not a commitment: revenue sharing depends on agreements with PSPs, set with the pilot programme partners. One basis point is 0.01% of volume.
v11.faq.6.a: The intended model: PSPs pay a fee on the volume Meridian brings them, on the same terms for all, and a share goes to the software vendor. It is being set with the pilot programme partners. The merchant pays Meridian nothing extra, and Meridian never touches the funds.
v11.faq.7.a: That Meridian never sends the same payment twice, and that every payment is proven by a signed journal you can check. Contractual commitments (service level, incident handling) are set with the pilot programme partners.
v11.faq.n.q: Does Meridian affect my till's NF525 certification?
v11.faq.n.a: Meridian does not touch the till's receipts, totals or fiscal archives: it passes on the payment order and returns its outcome. Ask your certification body to confirm the scope for your version.
v11.faq.o.a: With an installed till, the agent drives the terminal locally: payments work as long as the terminal can reach its bank. With an online till, the till must reach Meridian; if the store agent is offline, nothing is sent and the backup PSP chosen by the merchant can take over.
v11.faq.t.q: Which terminals and PSPs work today?
v11.faq.t.a: Available: Stripe Terminal. Being validated on real hardware: Caisse-AP over IP, ZVT and nexo terminals through the store agent, and Tap to Pay. In preparation: Adyen, Mollie, Square, SumUp and Viva. The pilot programme sets the order of the next ones.
v11.faq.s.q: Who provides support when the cashier calls?
v11.faq.s.a: The software vendor or reseller keeps first-line support, with the console: every payment has its journal there, step by step. Meridian provides second-line support on the connector and the agent. The PSP stays responsible for the terminal, acceptance and funds.
v11.faq.i.a: Five calls with the SDK, in the sandbox from day one. The pilot programme measures the real time to the first live payment; we will publish it.

v11.psp.title: Connect to tills without one integration per software vendor.
v11.psp.q.h: What your teams will ask us.
v11.psp.q1.p: The terminal's payment application stays yours, with its certifications. Meridian drives it from the outside, through your APIs or the till protocols.
v11.psp.q2.p: The store agent only connects outbound, never sees a card or PIN, and records every order before sending it.
v11.psp.q3.p: First line with the software vendor or reseller, second line with Meridian on the connector. You keep the terminal, acceptance and funds.
v11.psp.q4.p: A place among the first modules in the catalogue, and access to the software vendors and resellers in the pilot programme.
v11.res.title: Equip your customers with integrated payments, without a project per till.
v11.res.lede: Your customers arrive with their own terminal, bank or PSP. With Meridian you install the same agent everywhere and the till connects, locally or from the cloud.
v11.res.s1.p: On a store computer or inside the kiosk. It connects outbound: no port to open, no IP address to give to the cloud till.
v11.res.s2.p: Caisse-AP over IP, ZVT or nexo: the terminal's address and ID. The agent checks it is talking to the right terminal.
v11.res.s3.p: Installed till: the agent's local API. Online till: the Meridian API, which relays to the agent. The same five calls.
v11.res.s4.p: The console shows each point of sale, its terminal, its PSP and the journal of every payment.

v11.res.sell.2: Switching terminal or PSP, with no redevelopment
v11.res.sell.3: Proof for every payment in a dispute or an end-of-day gap
v11.res.status: The agent is being validated on real hardware: the pilot programme starts with a few resellers.
v11.res.cta.h: Let's equip your next store together.
